mainTopic: Burning a שטר and דינא דגרמי; returning stolen items that became forbidden or changed; a craftsman's liability and אומן קונה בשבח כלי
overview: The amud opens with רבה's ruling that someone who burns another person's שטר is פטור. רבא explains that the case is one where the burner admits what the שטר said. רב דימי בר חנינא ties the ruling to the מחלוקת between רבי שמעון and רבנן about דבר הגורם לממון. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע objects that רבי שמעון may have meant only items with real value of their own, like stolen חמץ. אמימר then rules that the burner pays the full debt according to the view that holds people liable for דינא דגרמי, and רפרם made רב אשי pay the full amount. Next, the גמרא asks who holds that a robber may return a forbidden item, like חמץ after פסח, saying 'הרי שלך לפניך'. רב חסדא's answer, רבי יעקב, is rejected, and a ברייתא shows that even the רבנן agree. רב פפא settles the case of rotten fruit: if all of it rotted, the robber pays, and if only part rotted, he returns it. A new משנה makes craftsmen pay for damaging items given to them for repair. רב אסי says this applies only to finished items and not to things the craftsman built from raw wood, because אומן קונה בשבח כלי. The גמרא's attempts to prove or disprove רב אסי from the משנה end without a decision, and it begins a new attempt from the case of wool given to a dyer.

steps.title: What case is רבה talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how burning a שטר could cause any loss. If witnesses exist, a new שטר can be written. If no witnesses exist, we cannot know what it said.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there are witnesses who know what was written in the document, let them write him a new, proper document! And if there are no witnesses, how do we know what was in it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the case behind רבה's ruling about burning a שטר. Either way, it seems there is nothing to discuss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If witnesses remember the שטר, the lender loses nothing, because the witnesses can write a new one. If there are no witnesses, a court could never charge the burner, because nobody knows the amount. So the גמרא asks what real case רבה could mean.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses
A document, here a document of debt (שטר)
Proper, good, valid
How do we know?

phrases.english: If there are witnesses
who know what was in the document,
let them write him a proper document!
And if there are no witnesses,
how do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דְּאִיכָּא סָהֲדִי דְּיָדְעִי מַאי הֲוָה בִּשְׁטָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of רבה's ruling, which was stated before this section, that burning a שטר is פטור.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case behind רבה's ruling about burning a שטר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Either there is no loss, because witnesses can rewrite the שטר, or the court has no way of knowing the amount. So there seems to be no real case to rule on.

steps.title: The burner believes the lender
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the case is where the burner admits to what the lender says was written in the שטר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Let it be a case where he believes him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a case that answers the question. The burner trusts the lender's word about what the שטר said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we know the amount, because the burner admits it, and the lender does lose out, because there are no witnesses to write a new שטר. Even so, רבה rules the burner is פטור. The loss is caused by the debt, and the debt is not something inside the paper itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be (the case is)
Where he believes him

phrases.english: רבא said:
Let it be where he believes him.
phrases.notes: He means the one who burned it believes the lender about what the שטר said.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: תְּהֵא בְּמַאֲמִינוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1 by describing a workable case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There seemed to be no case where the amount is known and the lender really loses.
steps.terutzMaskana: The burner admits the amount, so the amount is known and there is a real loss. רבה still says he is פטור.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה's case: someone burns a שטר and admits what it said. Even so, he does not have to pay.

steps.title: רבה's ruling depends on a famous מחלוקת
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי בר חנינא says רבה's ruling depends on the מחלוקת between רבי שמעון and רבנן about whether a דבר הגורם לממון counts as money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי בר חנינא said: This ruling of רבה is a מחלוקת between רבי שמעון and the רבנן. According to רבי שמעון, who says something that causes money counts as money, he is liable. According to the רבנן, who say something that causes money does not count as money, he is not liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי בר חנינא ties רבה's ruling to an older מחלוקת between תנאים. According to him, רבה holds like the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שטר is just paper. What makes it worth something is that it lets the lender collect money. רבי שמעון says something like that counts as money, so burning it would make the burner liable. The רבנן say it does not count as money, so he would be פטור, and that matches רבה's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute
Something that only causes money to be gained or lost, without being worth money itself
It is considered like money
He holds the person liable to pay

phrases.english: רב דימי בר חנינא said:
This ruling of רבה,
is a dispute between רבי שמעון and the רבנן.
According to רבי שמעון, who says

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר הַגּוֹרֵם לְמָמוֹן כְּמָמוֹן דָּמֵי – מְחַיֵּיב;
phrases.english: something that causes money is considered like money, he holds him liable;
according to the רבנן, who say

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר הַגּוֹרֵם לְמָמוֹן לָאו כְּמָמוֹן דָּמֵי – לָא מְחַיֵּיב.
phrases.english: something that causes money is not considered like money, he does not hold him liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב דִּימִי בַּר חֲנִינָא: הָא דְּרַבָּה מַחֲלוֹקֶת רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבָּנַן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רבה's case is clear, a new question opens: is his ruling something everyone agrees to, or does it depend on a מחלוקת?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה's ruling that the burner is פטור follows the רבנן. According to רבי שמעון the burner would be liable.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this is right, רבה's ruling is not something everyone agrees to. It depends on which side of the מחלוקת we follow.

steps.title: Maybe רבי שמעון only meant items with real value
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע objects. Maybe רבי שמעון said a דבר הגורם לממון counts as money only when the item itself has real value, as in רבה's case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, son of רב יהושע, objected: Say you heard רבי שמעון say that something that causes money counts as money, but only about an item that is basically worth money, like the case of רבה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע starts to argue against רב דימי. He is setting up a difference between two kinds of items, and he will support it with a case from רבה in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא suggests that רבי שמעון's rule may be limited. It may apply only to an item that is worth money on its own, such as food. A שטר is only paper, so רבי שמעון might agree that burning it is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it
Say you heard him (rule this way), but only in a certain case
Whose basic nature is money; something worth money on its own

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: רב הונא, son of רב יהושע, objected to it:
Say that you heard רבי שמעון say
something that causes money is considered like money,
about an item that is basically money, like the case of רבה;
phrases.notes: This is a different ruling of רבה, about stolen חמץ. The גמרא quotes it next.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: אֵימַר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 3 that רבי שמעון would hold the burner of a שטר liable.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי בר חנינא's claim that רבה's ruling depends on the מחלוקת between רבי שמעון and רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון's rule may only cover items that are worth money themselves. If so, a שטר would not be included, and even רבי שמעון could agree with רבה.

steps.title: רבה's case of stolen חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבה. If someone burns stolen חמץ during פסח, he is פטור. If he burns it after פסח, it depends on the מחלוקת between רבי שמעון and רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבה said: If someone stole חמץ before פסח, and another person came and burned it during the festival, he is exempt, because everyone is commanded to destroy it. After פסח, it is a dispute between רבי שמעון and the רבנן. According to רבי שמעון, who says something that causes money is like money, he is liable. According to the רבנן, who say it is not like money, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא brings רבה's ruling about stolen חמץ. It shows a case where the מחלוקת of רבי שמעון and רבנן clearly applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During פסח, burning the חמץ is a מצוה, so the burner is פטור. After פסח the חמץ may not be used. Still, the thief could have returned it as it was and been done, but now that it is burned he must pay its full value. That is why רבי שמעון holds the burner liable. The point is that חמץ was once real, valuable food, unlike a piece of paper.

keyTerms.meaning: He stole (by force or openly)
Leavened food, forbidden on פסח
During the festival (here, during פסח)
To destroy it (getting rid of חמץ)
Exempt, does not have to pay

phrases.english: As רבה said:
If someone stole חמץ before פסח,
and another person came and burned it during the festival, he is exempt,
because everyone is commanded to destroy it.
If he burned it after פסח,
it is a dispute between רבי שמעון and the רבנן;
according to רבי שמעון, who says

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר הַגּוֹרֵם לְמָמוֹן כְּמָמוֹן דָּמֵי – חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: something that causes money is considered like money, he is liable,
according to the רבנן, who say

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר הַגּוֹרֵם לְמָמוֹן לָאו כְּמָמוֹן דָּמֵי – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: something that causes money is not considered like money, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה: גָּזַל חָמֵץ לִפְנֵי הַפֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the ruling of רבה that step 4 referred to with the word כדרבה.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון's rule is known to apply to an item that is worth money on its own
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה's ruling about someone who burns stolen חמץ after פסח
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two rulings of רבה. The first is about burning a שטר, and there he says the burner is פטור. This one is a different ruling, about burning stolen חמץ.

steps.title: Does the rule apply to a mere piece of paper?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא ends his objection. For an item that is not worth money on its own, like a שטר, do we really say רבי שמעון holds it counts as money?
steps.simpleTranslation: But for an item that is not basically money, do we say this?
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes רב הונא's objection to רב דימי. The question is a challenge: no proof shows רבי שמעון applies his rule to a שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חמץ is real food, while a שטר is only paper with no value of its own. So רבי שמעון might agree that burning a שטר is פטור. If so, רבה's ruling could fit everyone, not only the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose basic nature is not money; something with no value of its own
Do we really say? (a challenging question)

phrases.aramaic: בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵין עִיקָּרוֹ מָמוֹן מִי אָמְרִינַן?
phrases.english: About an item that is not basically money, do we say this?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵין עִיקָּרוֹ מָמוֹן מִי אָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the חמץ case from step 5 to finish the challenge that began in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי בר חנינא's claim that רבי שמעון would hold the burner of a שטר liable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The only known case of רבי שמעון's rule involves an item worth money on its own (חמץ). A שטר is not like that, so we cannot assume רבי שמעון disagrees with רבה.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא splits things into two groups. An item worth money on its own, like חמץ, is where רבי שמעון's rule clearly applies. An item that is just paper, like a שטר, may not be covered, so רבה's ruling might fit even רבי שמעון.

steps.title: אמימר: The amount depends on whether one holds people liable for indirect damage
steps.stepSummary: אמימר rules that someone who burns a שטר pays the full debt if the judge holds by דינא דגרמי. If the judge does not hold by it, he pays only for the paper.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: A judge who holds people liable for indirect damage makes the burner pay the full value of the שטר, meaning the whole debt. A judge who does not hold people liable for indirect damage makes him pay only for the paper.
steps.whatsHappening: After all the back-and-forth, אמימר gives a clear rule for how much someone pays when he burns another person's שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning a שטר does not directly destroy the money. It only makes the debt hard to collect, so it is indirect damage. If you hold people liable for דינא דגרמי, the burner pays the whole debt. If not, he only pays for the piece of paper he burned.

keyTerms.meaning: The rule that a person is liable for damage he caused indirectly
A proper, valid document, meaning the full debt written in it
Just the paper itself

steps.whyThisMatters: This makes the practical result of the whole שטר discussion depend on one known question: whether one holds people liable for דינא דגרמי.

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
The one who rules by the law of indirect damage
collects in this case the value of a proper document,
phrases.notes: He means the full amount of the debt written in the שטר.

phrases.english: and the one who does not rule by the law of indirect damage
collects in this case merely the value of the paper.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַמֵּימָר: מַאן דְּדָאֵין דִּינָא דְּגַרְמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's objection, the גמרא gives a practical ruling that ties the amount to דינא דגרמי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who burns a שטר pays the full debt according to the view that holds people liable for indirect damage. According to the view that does not, he pays only for the paper.

steps.title: A real case: רפרם makes רב אשי pay the full value
steps.stepSummary: In a real case, רפרם forced רב אשי to pay, and he collected as if a valuable beam had been destroyed. That means the full value.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a real case, and רפרם forced רב אשי to pay. He made him pay like someone who ruined a fine beam meant for making a statue, meaning the full value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows how the ruling was actually applied in court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רפרם did not let the payment be just the cost of paper. He collected the full value, like a costly beam ready for a sculptor. This shows that in practice they held people liable for דינא דגרמי in this case.

keyTerms.meaning: A real-life case or incident
He forced him to pay
A beam meant for making a sculpture, which is a costly item

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, someone who burns a שטר pays the full debt, following דינא דגרמי, as רפרם ruled against רב אשי.

phrases.english: There was an incident
and Rafram forced Rav Ashi,
and he collected from him in this case like a beam for a sculpture.
phrases.notes: Think of a fine, expensive beam a sculptor would use. He paid the full value, not just for the paper.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה עוֹבָדָא וְכַפְיֵיהּ רַפְרָם לְרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the practical application of אמימר's rule, following the view that holds people liable for דינא דגרמי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The court collected the full value of the שטר from the one who burned it.

steps.title: Who holds that a forbidden item can be returned as is?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about stolen חמץ after פסח and asks which תנא holds that a robber can return an item that is now forbidden for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: If someone stole חמץ and פסח passed, the robber can say to the owner, 'Here is yours in front of you.' Which תנא holds that you can return an item that is forbidden for benefit and say, 'Here is yours in front of you'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes a line from the משנה and asks whose opinion it follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After פסח, חמץ is forbidden for benefit, so it is worth nothing. Even so, the משנה lets the robber just hand it back. The גמרא wants to know which תנא holds that returning a worthless forbidden item still counts as returning what was stolen.

keyTerms.meaning: Leavened food, which is forbidden for benefit once פסח has passed over it
Items that one may not get any benefit from
Here is yours in front of you. The robber returns the item as it is now.
Which תנא taught this?

phrases.english: Leavened bread, and Passover passed over it
he says to him: Here is yours before you.
Who is the tanna who taught
that with items forbidden for benefit we say
'Here is yours before you'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תַּנָּא אוֹמְרִין בְּאִיסּוּרֵי הֲנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The שטר topic is finished. The גמרא opens a new question on the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a robber can return an item that is now forbidden for benefit and say 'הרי שלך לפניך'?

steps.title: רב חסדא: It is רבי יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the משנה follows רבי יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: This is the opinion of רבי יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא names the תנא behind the משנה's rule. Next he will bring a ברייתא to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's claim is that רבי יעקב is the one who holds you can return a forbidden item as it is. The proof is coming in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who רב חסדא says is the source of the משנה's rule

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
It is Rabbi Yaakov.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of which תנא the משנה follows.

steps.title: The ברייתא about an ox that killed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists what happens to a שור שהמית before and after its sentence. רבי יעקב says that even after the sentence, a שומר who returns it has properly returned it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the ברייתא teaches: An ox that killed a person. Before it was sentenced: if the owner sold it, the sale works. If he made it holy, it is holy. If he slaughtered it, the meat is permitted. If a שומר returned it to the owner, it counts as returned. After it was sentenced: if he sold it, the sale does not work. If he made it holy, it is not holy. If he slaughtered it, the meat is forbidden. If a שומר returned it to the owner, it does not count as returned. רבי יעקב says: Even after it was sentenced, if a שומר returned it to the owner, it counts as returned.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא brings a ברייתא as his proof. It describes an ox that killed a person, before and after the court sentenced it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the ox is sentenced, it becomes forbidden for benefit and is worth nothing. So the רבנן say a שומר who hands it back has not really returned anything. רבי יעקב disagrees only on that last point and says the return still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: An ox that killed a person, which the court must sentence to be stoned
Its sentence was finished, meaning the court has ruled against it
He made it holy, giving it to the בית המקדש
A person watching an item or animal for its owner
It counts as returned

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יעקב does not argue about selling, making holy, or slaughtering after the sentence. He argues only about the שומר returning the ox.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
An ox that killed a person;
before its sentence was finished,
if he sold it, it is sold,
if he consecrated it, it is consecrated,
if he slaughtered it, its meat is permitted,
if a guardian returned it to its owner, it is returned.
Once its sentence was finished,
if he sold it, it is not sold,
if he consecrated it, it is not consecrated,
if he slaughtered it, its meat is forbidden,
if a guardian returned it to its owner, it is not returned.
Rabbi Yaakov says:
Even once its sentence was finished,
if a guardian returned it to its owner, it is returned.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: שׁוֹר שֶׁהֵמִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the source רב חסדא brings to back up his answer.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's claim that the משנה follows רבי יעקב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a שור שהמית that a שומר returned after its sentence

steps.title: The argument is about returning a forbidden item
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא finishes his proof. רבי יעקב and the רבנן must be arguing about whether a forbidden item can be returned with 'הרי שלך לפניך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not that they argue about this? רבי יעקב holds that with items forbidden for benefit, you can say 'Here is yours in front of you.' The רבנן hold that with items forbidden for benefit, you cannot say 'Here is yours in front of you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא explains what the argument in the ברייתא is about. This finishes his proof that the משנה follows רבי יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sentenced ox is forbidden for benefit, just like חמץ after פסח. רבי יעקב says the שומר's return counts, so he must hold that a forbidden item can be returned as it is. That matches the משנה, while the רבנן hold that it cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not so that...? A way of suggesting how to read a source
They argue about
The Sages who disagree with רבי יעקב

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא says the משנה about חמץ after פסח follows רבי יעקב. In his view, רבי יעקב holds that a forbidden item can be returned with 'הרי שלך לפניך,' and the רבנן disagree.

phrases.english: What, is it not about this that they argue,
that Rabbi Yaakov holds:
with items forbidden for benefit we say 'Here is yours before you,'
and the Rabbis hold:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אוֹמְרִין בְּאִיסּוּרֵי הֲנָאָה ״הֲרֵי שֶׁלְּךָ לְפָנֶיךָ״?
phrases.english: with items forbidden for benefit we do not say 'Here is yours before you'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי, לָאו בְּהָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא that proves רב חסדא's answer.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה about חמץ after פסח follows רבי יעקב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The argument between רבי יעקב and the רבנן about a שומר returning a sentenced ox

steps.title: רבה rejects רב חסדא's reading of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבה says everyone agrees that a forbidden item can be returned with 'הרי שלך לפניך'. Otherwise the תנאים should have argued about חמץ on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: No. Everyone agrees that with items forbidden for benefit we say 'here is yours before you.' If they really argued about that, they should have argued about חמץ on פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה pushes back on רב חסדא's proof from Step 12. He says רבי יעקב and the רבנן are not arguing about איסורי הנאה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the argument were about returning any forbidden item, the clearest example would be חמץ בפסח. Since the ברייתא used a שור instead, the argument must be about something special to the ox. This means the משנה about חמץ can follow everyone, even the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: No. It signals a rejection.
Everyone agrees
Items you are not allowed to benefit from
For if so (an argument from what would follow)

phrases.english: Rabba said to him: No.
Everyone agrees that we say,
with items forbidden for benefit, 'Here is yours before you.'
For if so, they should have argued about chametz on Pesach.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב חסדא's conclusion from Step 12
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the ברייתא's argument is about returning איסורי הנאה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If that were the argument, the ברייתא should have used חמץ בפסח as the example, not an ox

steps.title: רבה gives a new reason for the argument
steps.stepSummary: רבה says the real argument is whether an ox can be sentenced when it is not present.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה said: Here they argue about whether an ox can be sentenced not in its presence.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting רב חסדא's reading, רבה offers his own explanation of what the ברייתא is arguing about. The next two steps will explain each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new question is a court procedure question, not a question about forbidden items. Can a בית דין sentence the ox when the ox is not standing before it? This explains why the ברייתא chose an ox as its example.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It introduces a new approach.
Finish its sentence (the court's final ruling)
Not in its presence
They argue

phrases.english: Rather, Rabba said:
Here, about sentencing an ox
not in its presence, they argue.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבָּה: הָכָא בְּגוֹמְרִין דִּינוֹ שֶׁל שׁוֹר שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reading Step 13 rejected with a new one
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the argument to a different issue
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא argues about returning איסורי הנאה
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא argues about sentencing an ox in its absence

steps.title: The רבנן's view: an ox cannot be sentenced in its absence
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן hold that an ox cannot be sentenced in its absence. So the owner can claim the שומר handed it to a court he could not escape.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold that an ox is not sentenced in its absence. The owner says to the שומר: If you had brought it to me, I would have chased it off to the marsh. Now you handed it to someone I can't win a case against!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the רבנן's side. Because the ox had to be present to be sentenced, the שומר's handing it over is what caused the sentence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the court needs the ox in front of it, the owner could have saved the ox by hiding it. The שומר took away that chance by giving it to the court. That is why he must pay and cannot just return the forbidden ox.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have chased it away
The marsh
To argue a case in court

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין גּוֹמְרִין דִּינוֹ שֶׁל שׁוֹר שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו,
phrases.english: We do not sentence an ox when it is not present,
for the owner says to him: If you had brought it to me,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the שומר, the guard who was watching the ox.

phrases.english: I would have chased it away to the marsh.
Now you have handed it over to someone
I cannot argue my case against!
phrases.notes: He means the court. Once the ox is there, he has no way to stop the sentence.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: אֵין גּוֹמְרִין דִּינוֹ שֶׁל שׁוֹר שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the רבנן's side of רבה's new reading
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ox is not sentenced in its absence, so the שומר who handed it over must pay

steps.title: רבי יעקב's view: an ox can be sentenced in its absence
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב holds that an ox can be sentenced in its absence. So the שומר can say he caused no loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב holds that an ox can be sentenced in its absence. The שומר says: What did I do to it? In the end they would have sentenced it even without it there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי יעקב's side. Since the court could sentence the ox without it being present, the שומר did not cause the sentence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hiding the ox would not have helped, because the court could rule anyway. So the שומר did no damage, and he may return the ox as is. רבה's point is that this is why רבי יעקב lets him return it, not a general rule about forbidden items.

keyTerms.meaning: What did I do to it?
In the end, either way

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה, the ברייתא's argument is about court procedure for an ox. Everyone agrees that a forbidden item like חמץ can be returned as is.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ya'akov holds:

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹמְרִין דִּינוֹ שֶׁל שׁוֹר שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו,
phrases.english: We do sentence an ox when it is not present,
for the guard says to him: What did I do to it?

phrases.aramaic: סוֹף סוֹף הֲוָה גָּמְרִי לֵיהּ (דִּינָא) [לְדִינֵיהּ] שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו.
phrases.english: In the end they would have finished its sentence without it present.
phrases.notes: Some versions say the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean the same thing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב סָבַר: גּוֹמְרִין דִּינוֹ שֶׁל שׁוֹר שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יעקב's side, completing רבה's explanation
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ox can be sentenced in its absence, so the שומר caused no loss and may return it

steps.title: רב חסדא asks רבה בר שמואל about forbidden items
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא meets רבה בר שמואל and asks if he learned any source about איסורי הנאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא found רבה בר שמואל and said to him: Did you learn anything about items forbidden for benefit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story. רב חסדא asks another scholar for a source, and this sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא is looking for a teaching about whether a stolen item that became forbidden can be returned. The answer will bring a direct source on that question.

keyTerms.meaning: He found him
Did you learn (a ברייתא)?
Anything

phrases.aramaic: אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל,
phrases.english: Rav Chisda found Rabba bar Shmuel.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תְּנֵית מִידֵּי בְּאִיסּוּרֵי הֲנָאָה?
phrases.english: He said to him: Did you learn anything about items forbidden for benefit?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story that returns to the question about איסורי הנאה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is there a taught source about returning stolen items that became forbidden for benefit?

steps.title: The verse teaches: return the same item you stole
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שמואל quotes a ברייתא. The words 'אשר גזל' teach that the robber returns the same item he stole.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Yes, we learned: 'And he shall return the stolen item.' Why does the verse add 'that he stole'? He returns the same thing he stole.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר שמואל answers yes and quotes a ברייתא. It reads extra words in the פסוק as a lesson about returning the item itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'אשר גזל' looks unnecessary, so the ברייתא learns from it. The robber gives back the actual item he took, even if it has changed. The next step lists the cases this covers.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall return the stolen item (ויקרא 5:23)
Why does the verse say this? (the words seem extra)
The same item that he stole

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes, we learned:
'And he shall return the stolen item.'
Why does the verse say 'that he stole'?
He returns the same thing he stole.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין, תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חסדא's question from Step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא learns from 'אשר גזל' that the robber returns the actual item he stole

steps.title: List of changed items the robber may return as is
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists items that spoiled or became forbidden, including חמץ after פסח. The robber may still say 'הרי שלך לפניך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: If he stole a coin and it was taken out of use, fruit and it rotted, wine and it soured, תרומה and it became impure, חמץ and פסח passed, an animal and a sin was done with it, or an ox before its sentence was finished, he says to him: Here is yours before you.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by listing cases where the robber returns the item even though it lost value or became forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list includes items that are now אסור בהנאה, like חמץ after פסח. That gives the source רב חסדא asked for: a forbidden item can be returned as is. The ox is listed only before its sentence, which fits the earlier discussion about a sentenced ox.

keyTerms.meaning: From here they said
Was taken out of use (a coin)
Turned sour
A sin was done with it
Here is yours before you (take it back as it is)

steps.whatToRemember: A robber returns the same item he stole, even if it spoiled or became forbidden, like חמץ after פסח. He says 'הרי שלך לפניך'.

phrases.english: From here they said:
If he stole a coin and it was taken out of use,
fruit and it rotted, wine and it turned sour,
terumah and it became impure,
chametz and Pesach passed over it,
an animal and a sin was done with it,
or an ox before its sentence was finished,
he says to him: 'Here is yours before you.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ: גָּזַל מַטְבֵּעַ וְנִפְסַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and spells out which cases the rule covers
steps.raayaObject: That a stolen item that became forbidden for benefit can be returned as is
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's list, which includes חמץ after פסח

steps.title: Even the Rabbis allow returning forbidden חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The view that an ox that killed can be returned before sentencing but not after belongs to the רבנן. Yet the ברייתא teaches that חמץ after פסח is returned as is. This undercuts רב חסדא's earlier assumption.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who did we hear say that before the ox's sentence it can be returned, but after the sentence it cannot? The רבנן. Yet the ברייתא teaches that with חמץ that stayed over פסח, the robber can say, 'Here is yours before you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem. The ברייתא that רבה בר שמואל just quoted clashes with how רב חסדא had read the opinion of the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא allows returning the ox only before its sentence, which is the view of the רבנן. So the ברייתא follows the רבנן, and yet it says forbidden חמץ after פסח is returned as is. That disproves רב חסדא's claim that the רבנן hold a forbidden item cannot be returned as is.

keyTerms.meaning: its verdict was finished (the ox was sentenced by the court)
the Rabbis (the majority opinion against רבי יעקב)
and it teaches (introduces a quote from the ברייתא)
leavened food that stayed in a Jew's ownership over פסח, which is forbidden to benefit from

phrases.english: Whom have you heard who says:
before its verdict was finished, yes,
phrases.notes: This means the ox that killed a person, from the earlier steps. Before it is sentenced, it can be returned as is.

phrases.english: after its verdict was finished, no?
The Rabbis;
and yet it teaches: leavened bread that פסח passed over,
he says to him, 'Here is yours before you'!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from step 19 to challenge רב חסדא's reading of the רבנן in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's assumption that, according to the רבנן, a forbidden item cannot be returned as is
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lets the robber return forbidden חמץ as is. The רבנן would not argue with that, so their ruling about the sentenced ox must have a different reason.

steps.title: רב חסדא admits his mistake
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא accepts the proof and asks רבה בר שמואל not to tell the scholars about his earlier view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to him: If you meet them, don't say anything at all to them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives in. He asks that his earlier mistaken reading not be spread around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא does not offer an answer. His request shows he accepts that the ברייתא disproves his reading, so the question about איסורי הנאה is settled.

keyTerms.meaning: if you find them (meet the scholars)
and nothing at all

steps.whatToRemember: A robber may return חמץ that stayed over פסח and say 'הרי שלך לפניך'. Even the רבנן agree that a forbidden item is returned as is.

phrases.english: He said to him: If you find them,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the scholars. רב חסדא means: don't spread my mistaken idea.

phrases.english: do not say to them anything at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לְהוּ לָא תֵּימָא לְהוּ וְלָא מִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב חסדא accepts the challenge of step 20.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב חסדא's reading is dropped. A forbidden stolen item can be returned as is.

steps.title: Rotten fruit: the ברייתא against the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says rotten stolen fruit is returned as is. The משנה says the robber pays what the fruit was worth when he stole it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: fruit that rotted, he says to him 'Here is yours before you.' But we learned in the משנה: fruit that rotted, he pays according to the time of the robbery!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to another case in the same ברייתא, rotten fruit. It shows that this case seems to contradict the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the ברייתא, rotting does not change the fruit enough, so the owner takes it back as is. According to the משנה, rotting is a real change. The robber keeps the fruit and pays its original value, so the two sources seem to say opposite things.

keyTerms.meaning: and they rotted
but didn't we learn (in a משנה)? It introduces a contradiction.
according to the value at the time of the robbery

phrases.english: Fruit that rotted:
he says to him, 'Here is yours before you.'
But didn't we learn: fruit that rotted,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה earlier in the פרק, on 96b.

phrases.english: he pays according to the time of the robbery!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתְנַן: פֵּירוֹת וְהִרְקִיבוּ מְשַׁלֵּם כִּשְׁעַת הַגְּזֵילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the חמץ case to the rotten-fruit case in the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that rotten fruit is returned as is
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה treats rotting as a change that makes the robber pay the original value. That contradicts returning the fruit as is.

steps.title: רב פפא: all rotted or only part
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the משנה means all the fruit rotted, and the ברייתא means only part of it rotted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Here, all of them rotted; there, only some of them rotted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא settles the contradiction. The two sources are talking about different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When all the fruit rots, the change is big enough that the robber owns it and pays its value from the time of the robbery. When only part rots, the change is small, so he can hand back the fruit as is.

keyTerms.meaning: here ... there (each source is talking about a different case)
all of them
some of them

steps.whatToRemember: Fruit that fully rotted counts as changed, so the robber pays its original value. Fruit that only partly rotted is returned as is.

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
Here, where they all rotted,
phrases.notes: This first 'here' is the משנה, where he pays.

phrases.english: there, where some of them rotted.
phrases.notes: This second one is the ברייתא, where he returns the fruit as is.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: כָּאן שֶׁהִרְקִיבוּ כּוּלָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא seemed to rule differently on the same case of rotten fruit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means fruit that fully rotted, and the ברייתא means fruit that partly rotted.

steps.title: Craftsmen who damage items they were fixing
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that craftsmen who damage items given to them for repair must pay. The example is a carpenter fixing furniture.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone gave items to craftsmen to fix and they damaged them, they must pay. If he gave a carpenter a chest, a box or a cabinet to fix and he damaged it, he must pay.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It is about a craftsman's responsibility for damage he causes while doing his job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A craftsman is not excused just because the damage happened while he was working. If he ruins the item he was hired to fix, he pays for the damage.

keyTerms.meaning: craftsmen
carpenter (in this context, a woodworker)
a chest, a box and a cabinet (pieces of wooden furniture)
and they damaged (it)

steps.confusionAlert: Here חָרָשׁ means a carpenter, not a deaf person (חֵרֵשׁ), even though the letters are the same.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If one gave to craftsmen to fix,
and they damaged it, they are liable to pay.

phrases.aramaic: נָתַן לְחָרָשׁ שִׁידָּה תֵּיבָה וּמִגְדָּל לְתַקֵּן,
phrases.english: If he gave a carpenter a chest, a box or a cabinet to fix,
and he damaged it, he is liable to pay.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָתַן לָאוּמָּנִין לְתַקֵּן וְקִלְקְלוּ חַיָּיבִין לְשַׁלֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A craftsman who damages an item he was given to fix must pay.

steps.title: A builder taking down a wall
steps.stepSummary: A builder who breaks or damages the stones while taking down a wall must pay. If the wall falls on a different side, he is exempt, unless it fell because of his blow.
steps.simpleTranslation: A builder who agreed to take down a wall and broke or damaged the stones must pay. If he was taking it down on one side and it fell on another side, he is exempt. But if it fell because of the force of his blow, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a builder. It shows when he must pay and when he does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breaking the stones is damage caused by his own work, so he pays. A collapse on a different side is not his doing, so he is exempt. If his blow is what made it fall, then he caused it, and he pays.

keyTerms.meaning: builder
to take down the wall
because of the force of the blow

phrases.english: And the builder who took upon himself
to take down the wall,
and he broke the stones or damaged them,
is liable to pay.
If he was taking it down on this side
and it fell on another side, he is exempt;
but if it was because of the blow, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַבַּנַּאי שֶׁקִּיבֵּל עָלָיו לִסְתּוֹר אֶת הַכּוֹתֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second worker case to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A builder pays for damage his work causes. He is exempt when the wall falls on a side he was not working on, unless his blow caused it.

steps.title: רב אסי: fixing an existing item vs. building a new one
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי limits the משנה. The carpenter pays only when he broke an item he was fixing. If he built the item from the owner's wood and then broke it, he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב אסי said: They only taught this when someone gave a carpenter a chest, a box or a cabinet to drive a nail into, and he drove a nail in and broke them. But if he gave the carpenter wood to make a chest, a box or a cabinet, and he made them from it and broke them, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רב אסי. He narrows the carpenter's liability from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's case is a finished item brought in for repair, such as adding a nail, which the carpenter then broke. In that case he pays. If the carpenter himself made the item from the owner's wood and then broke it, רב אסי rules he is exempt. The line he draws is between repairing something that already existed and making something new.

keyTerms.meaning: they only taught this (the rule) in a case where...
to drive a nail into them
pieces of wood (raw material)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a craftsman's liability can depend on whether he received a finished item or raw material.

phrases.english: GEMARA: רב אסי said:
They taught this only where he gave a carpenter
a chest, a box or a cabinet
to drive a nail into them,
and he drove a nail into them and broke them;
but if he gave the carpenter wood
to make a chest, a box or a cabinet,
and he made from it a chest, a box or a cabinet
and broke them, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the carpenter case of the משנה in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A carpenter pays for breaking a finished item given to him for repair. He is exempt for breaking an item he built from the owner's wood.

steps.title: The reason behind רב אסי's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב אסי's exemption and answers that a craftsman acquires the improvement he adds to an item.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? A craftsman acquires through the improvement of the item.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב אסי exempts a carpenter who built an item from the owner's wood and then broke it. It answers that the craftsman owns the value he added.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The finished item's added value came from the craftsman's work, so until he hands it back, that value counts as his. When he breaks it, he is breaking his own improvement. He only has to pay back the raw wood.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Craftsman
Acquires, gains ownership
The improvement or added value of the item

steps.whyThisMatters: The principle אומן קונה בשבח כלי is the key idea that the rest of this section tests against the משנה.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
A craftsman acquires through the improvement of the item.
phrases.notes: He means the craftsman owns the extra value his work added.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? אוּמָּן קוֹנֶה בִּשְׁבַח כְּלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רב אסי's limitation in Step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is the carpenter exempt when he built the item from the owner's wood?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A craftsman acquires the improvement he adds to an item.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה: maybe it means raw wood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה's ruling that craftsmen pay is talking about raw wood, which would contradict רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: If one gave to craftsmen and they damaged, they are obligated to pay. What, is it not where he gave them wood?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה and asks whether it is talking about a case where the owner gave the craftsman raw wood. If so, that would go against רב אסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just says 'gave to craftsmen' and does not say what was given. If that includes raw wood that the craftsman built into an item and then broke, he would have to pay. That is the opposite of רב אסי's exemption.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned (in a משנה)
They damaged or ruined
Is it not so that (opens a suggested reading)
Raw wood

phrases.english: We learned in the משנה:
If one gave to craftsmen and they damaged,
they are obligated to pay.
What, is it not where he gave them wood?
phrases.notes: If even raw wood counts here, the craftsman pays, and that clashes with רב אסי.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: נָתַן לָאוּמָּנִין וְקִלְקְלוּ – חַיָּיבִין לְשַׁלֵּם. מַאי, לָאו דְּיָהֵיב לְהוּ עֵצִים?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אסי's ruling and its reason using the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's exemption for a craftsman who built and broke an item from the owner's wood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה makes craftsmen liable without saying what was given. If that includes raw wood, it directly contradicts רב אסי.

steps.title: No, the משנה means finished furniture
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about finished items like a chest, a box, or a cabinet, not raw wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, a chest, a box, and a cabinet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. The משנה is talking about finished furniture given in for repair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the item was already finished, the craftsman did not create its value. So אומן קונה בשבח כלי does not apply, and he pays. This fits with רב אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: A chest
A box
A cabinet

phrases.english: No, a chest, a box, and a cabinet.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, שִׁידָּה תֵּיבָה וּמִגְדָּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה might be talking about raw wood.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is talking about finished items given in for repair, so there is no contradiction with רב אסי.

steps.title: But the last part implies the first part is wood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the משנה lists the chest, box, and cabinet separately in its last part, which implies the first part means something else, namely raw wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the last part teaches 'a chest, a box, and a cabinet,' this implies the first part is wood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. The furniture is mentioned in a separate, later part of the משנה, so the first part must be about a different case: raw wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, when a משנה has a first part (רישא) and a last part (סיפא), each one teaches a different case. If the סיפא is about finished furniture, the רישא seems to be about raw wood. That brings back the contradiction with רב אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה
The first part of a משנה
It is implied, we can infer

phrases.english: But since the last part teaches:
a chest, a box, and a cabinet,
this implies that the first part is wood!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מִדְּקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא: שִׁידָּה תֵּיבָה וּמִגְדָּל, מִכְּלָל דְּרֵישָׁא – עֵצִים!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה is talking about finished furniture
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא names the furniture as its own case, so the רישא must be a different case, which would be raw wood.

steps.title: The last part explains the first part
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the סיפא is not a new case. It explains the רישא: 'How so? For example, he gave a carpenter a chest, a box, or a cabinet.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: It is explaining it. How so, if one gave to craftsmen to fix and they damaged, they must pay? For example, where he gave a carpenter a chest, a box, and a cabinet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the סיפא is an example that explains the רישא. It is not a separate case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the רישא and סיפא are one case: finished furniture brought in for repair. Nothing in the משנה is about raw wood, and רב אסי stands.

keyTerms.meaning: They say (introduces an answer)
It is explaining (the earlier part)
How so? In what case?
Carpenter, woodworker

steps.confusionAlert: Usually רישא and סיפא are two different cases. Here the גמרא says the סיפא is just an example that explains the רישא.

phrases.english: They say: It is explaining it:
How so, if one gave to craftsmen to fix
and they damaged, they must pay?
For example, where he gave a carpenter
a chest, a box, and a cabinet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: פָּרוֹשֵׁי קָא מְפָרֵשׁ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in Step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the structure of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא is a separate case, so the רישא is raw wood.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סיפא explains the רישא; both are about finished items brought in for repair.

steps.title: Proof that this reading is correct
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the 'explaining' reading makes sense. If the רישא meant raw wood and the craftsman still pays, then of course he pays for finished furniture, so the סיפא would be unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too it is logical that it teaches 'How so.' For if you think the first part is wood: now that it taught us that with wood they must pay, and we do not say a craftsman acquires through the improvement of items, is a chest, a box, and a cabinet even needed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer with logic. Reading the רישא as raw wood would make the סיפא pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Raw wood is the harder case for making the craftsman pay, because there he could claim he owns the improvement. If he pays even there, he would obviously pay for finished furniture. A משנה does not teach something that obvious, so the סיפא must be explaining the רישא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is logical, it makes sense
You might think
It taught us
Is it even needed? (it is obvious)

steps.whatToRemember: This step tries to prove that the סיפא only explains the רישא. The next step rejects this proof, so the משנה ends up proving nothing either way about רב אסי.

phrases.english: And so too it is logical
that it teaches "How so."
For if you think the first part is wood:
now that it taught us that with wood they must pay

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אָמְרִינַן אוּמָּן קוֹנֶה בִּשְׁבַח כֵּלִים;
phrases.english: and we do not say a craftsman acquires through the improvement of items,
is a chest, a box, and a cabinet even needed?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא – דְּ״כֵיצַד״ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in Step 31 with logical reasoning.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the סיפא explains the רישא
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: a משנה does not teach something that is obvious. If the רישא meant raw wood, the סיפא would be obvious and unnecessary.

steps.title: The last part of the משנה may be there to show the first part is about raw wood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 32. The סיפא could be teaching that the רישא is about raw wood, and the craftsman still pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: If that is your reason, it is no proof. The תנא taught the last part to shed light on the first part. Otherwise you might say the first part is about a chest, a box, or a cabinet, but not raw wood. So he taught the chest, box, and cabinet in the last part. That shows the first part is about raw wood, and even so the craftsman must pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 32. It shows that the סיפא can be read in a way that makes the רישא about raw wood after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 32 said a סיפא about finished furniture would be pointless if the רישא were about raw wood, so the סיפא must just explain the רישא. Here the גמרא flips it: the סיפא names the finished items so that the רישא will be understood as raw wood. That means the craftsman pays even for raw wood, so the משנה gives no proof for רב אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: It is no proof. That reason does not force the conclusion.
To reveal or shed light on
The first part / the last part of a משנה
By inference; it follows from this
And even so
Raw wood (not yet made into furniture)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה can be read either way: the סיפא may explain the רישא, or it may show that the רישא is about raw wood. Because both readings are possible, this משנה cannot prove רב אסי's view.
steps.confusionAlert: It looks backwards: the סיפא talks about finished furniture, yet it is used to prove the רישא is about raw wood. The idea is that naming the finished items separately in the סיפא leaves the רישא for something else, which is raw wood.

phrases.english: If it is because of this – it is no proof.
phrases.notes: "This" is the argument from step 32, that the סיפא would be unnecessary.

phrases.english: The תנא taught the last part to shed light on the first part,
so that you should not say:
the first part is about a chest, a box, or a cabinet –
but not raw wood;
so he taught in the last part: a chest, a box, or a cabinet –
which shows that the first part is about raw wood,
and even so he must pay.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִשּׁוּם הָא – לָא אִירְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 32 by offering a different reason the סיפא is needed.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the סיפא must only explain the רישא, which was the basis for using the משנה to support רב אסי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Step 32 assumed a סיפא about finished furniture would be pointless if the רישא meant raw wood. But the סיפא has a job: it makes clear that the רישא is about raw wood.
steps.whyThisMatters: It closes this line of discussion. The first משנה cannot decide the question about רב אסי, so the גמרא has to look for support elsewhere.

steps.title: A new attempt to support רב אסי from the case of wool given to a dyer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that another משנה, about giving wool to a dyer, might support רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say a משנה supports him: one who gives wool to a dyer,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is opening a new attempt to back up רב אסי. It starts quoting a משנה about wool given to a dyer, and the rest of the quote comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first משנה (the carpenter) turned out to be no help, so the גמרא turns to a different case. Only the opening words of the dyer משנה appear here, so the actual proof has not been made yet.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say; introduces a suggestion the גמרא will test
It supports him
Wool
A dyer

phrases.english: Let us say it supports him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רב אסי. The quote that follows is from a משנה later in this פרק.

phrases.english: one who gives wool to a dyer,

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the carpenter משנה gave no proof, the גמרא looks to a new משנה for support of רב אסי.
